Description
Keeper Security is hiring an experienced Senior Software Engineer to join our Privileged Access Management team and lead backend development for Discovery capabilities within KeeperPAM. This is a 100% remote position, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the Chicago, IL or El Dorado Hills, CA metro areas.
Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help build the systems that discover and secure privileged identities and infrastructure across complex enterprise environments.
About Keeper
Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.
About the Job
As a Senior Software Engineer on Keeper's PAM Discovery team, you will be a primary developer for the backend discovery service that identifies privileged accounts, service accounts, keys and machines across Active Directory, cloud IAM, databases and endpoints so they can be brought under secure management and rotation. This is primarily a backend engineering role, most of your time will be spent building services, data pipelines and integrations in Python, with some Java/Kotlin work on our cloud services and occasional changes to our TypeScript/React administrative interface.
What makes this problem interesting: Discovery runs on gateways deployed inside customer environments that Keeper cannot access directly, so the system has to be resilient, self-diagnosing and safe even when debugging access is limited and deployed versions vary. And Keeper's zero-knowledge architecture requires discovered data to be encrypted before it leaves the customer environment, which rules out most of the conventional answers for how that data can be processed, indexed and presented.
Responsibilities

• Design and develop the Python discovery engine that runs on customer-deployed gateways, and the Java/Kotlin cloud services that store and serve discovered data

• Build systems that discover privileged accounts, service accounts, keys, machines and related identity data across Active Directory, cloud IAM, databases and endpoints

• Solve identity correlation and reconciliation challenges, including determining when accounts discovered across multiple systems represent the same principal

• Build incremental re-scan and state-reconciliation capabilities that maintain an accurate view of customer environments without accumulating duplicate or stale data

• Build the test coverage and diagnostic tooling that let us trust code we can't debug in the field: unit, integration and automated tests, plus logging and error reporting good enough to root-cause an issue from a customer's logs alone

• Design discovery workflows that operate safely inside customer production networks, respecting API limits, limiting blast radius and remaining resilient to partial failures across large environments

• Develop secure data-processing workflows that operate within Keeper’s zero-knowledge architecture and protect discovered data throughout collection, transmission and storage

• Collaborate with Product, QA and other PAM engineers on technical design, testing, troubleshooting and delivery of Discovery features

title: Senior Google Ads Buyer, DTC eCommerce
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
That is the whole job.
Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
Google is where we are putting our next round of growth. You would own a set of those accounts end to end.
Here is what "end to end" actually means.
You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

Interested in creative tech career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design

Build digital products and services 0-1

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

The Senior Growth Manager will own local growth strategy and end-to-end program delivery across product go-to-market, customer growth, and priority segments, including advanced traders and VIPs.

 

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role responsible for translating business and product priorities into coordinated growth initiatives and measurable commercial outcomes. The role will act as the key local stakeholder for global Performance Marketing and Lifecycle teams while working closely with Product, Relationship Management, Data, Marketing, and other regional and global stakeholders.

 

What You'll be Doing

Own local product and lifecycle marketing initiatives end to end, from strategy and positioning through execution, journey optimization, and performance reporting .

•
Lead product marketing and go-to-market programs for priority products, defining positioning, target segments, customer journeys, value propositions, messaging, and adoption metrics .

•
Develop full-funnel lifecycle strategies for advanced traders, VIPs, high-value customers, and other priority segments, driving activation, feature adoption, retention, monetization, and lifetime value .

Design customer lifecycle, loyalty, reward, engagement, and reactivation programs that drive long-term retention and commercial growth .

•
Act as the key local stakeholder for global Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, and Lifecycle teams, translating local product priorities into campaign briefs, automated journeys, and tailored messaging .

•
Plan and execute high-value customer events, VIP experiences, partner activations, and lifecycle engagements, managing delivery from objectives and budgets through to stakeholder coordination and retention reporting .

•
Partner with Product, Data, Relationship Management, Marketing, Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Finance to deliver coordinated, compliant, and user-centric lifecycle programs .

•
Monitor funnel conversion, product adoption, and lifecycle performance, identify retention and growth opportunities, and communicate insights and recommendations to stakeholders .

What We Look For In You  

•
Minimum 5 years of experience in product marketing, lifecycle marketing, CRM strategy, retention growth, or a related field .

•
Proven experience managing product marketing, go-to-market, or lifecycle initiatives from strategy through execution and performance reporting .

•
Strong understanding of customer segmentation, lifecycle journeys, retention, reactivation, messaging, and product positioning .

•
Deep understanding of lifecycle marketing principles and tools, with the ability to build automated user journeys and brief/collaborate effectively with specialist teams .

•
Experience planning and executing VIP engagements, targeted customer events, partner activations, or lifecycle-driven experiences .

•
Strong commercial and analytical skills, with the ability to connect lifecycle and product marketing activities to retention and business outcomes .

•
Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders-especially Product and Engineering teams-and work effectively with regional and global teams .

•
Strong communication, stakeholder-management

description:
About Terawatt Infrastructure
The once in a century transition to autonomous and electric vehicles is underway and will require a multi-trillion-dollar investment in energy and charging infrastructure, and the real estate to site it on. Terawatt is the leader in delivering large scale, turnkey charging solutions for companies rapidly deploying AV and EV fleets. Whether it’s an urban mobility hub, or a carefully located multi-fleet hub for semi-trucks, Terawatt brings the talent, capabilities, and capital to create reliable, cost-effective solutions for customers on the leading edge of the transition to the next generation of transport.
With a growing portfolio of sites across the US in urban hubs and along key logistics and transportation corridors. Terawatt is building the permanent transportation and logistics infrastructure of tomorrow through a robust combination of capital, real estate, development, and site operations solutions. The company develops, finances, owns, and operates charging solutions that take the cost and complexity out of electrifying fleets. 
Our Values
Six core values guide how we work: commitments we make to each other. Our pace is set by a simple conviction: imperfect action beats perfect inaction, so we move with purpose, adapt without ego, and measure ourselves by progress rather than activity. Ownership travels with autonomy. Your name is on the work, and the best answer wins the conversation, wherever it lives. That candor works because of what surrounds it: people who show up with intention and have each other's back, tough on ideas and generous with people. Our customers feel this as reliability earned daily, every interaction treated as a chance to build something lasting. And underneath it all is why the work matters. The climate doesn't wait, and the stakes are also human: behind every checklist and every inspection is a person going home safely. We call it "This work has a heartbeat” - it's what the other five rest on.
Our Technology
Terawatt is not a traditional infrastructure operator. Our technology platform transforms a portfolio of sites into a reliable, intelligent network - through advanced power management, operational optimization, and data-driven systems that back our customers with hard performance guarantees. That's what makes us a de-risked operator and a category-defining company.
We sit at a rare intersection: software, hardware, real estate, energy systems, and live site operations. The work is concrete and the stakes are real. The code you write today runs physical infrastructure tomorrow. You'll build systems that orchestrate megawatts of power across hundreds of chargers, ingest millions of telemetry events per day, and keep autonomous fleets, rideshare vehicles, and heavy-duty trucks moving - in real time.

Compensation for this role is determined by several factors, including the cost of labor in specific geographic markets, and these ranges are intended to provide a helpful reference. The actual compensation offer will be based on the candidate’s location, skills, level of expertise and experience, and internal equity considerations. In addition to base salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package and, where applicable, performance-based incentives.

We are building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. At Terawatt, we continuously strive to foster inclusion, humility, energizing relationships, and belonging, and welcome new ideas. We're growing and want you to grow with us. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager
description:

Ditto is redefining how data moves at the edge. Our mission is to make it seamless for developers to build resilient, real-time applications, regardless of network conditions. Whether you're in a stadium, airplane, or remote military base, Ditto's peer-to-peer sync engine ensures devices stay connected and data stays consistent, even without internet. With more than $145 million in funding and trusted by organizations like Chick-fil-A, Delta Airlines, and the U.S. military, Ditto powers mission-critical experiences across aviation, retail, travel, hospitality, defense, and more. As a globally distributed, fast-growing startup, we’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive team that reflects the wide range of perspectives needed to solve the world’s hardest connectivity problems.

Ditto's enterprise customers are building infrastructure on top of our platform. That means post-sales at Ditto is about delivery, not just adoption. As a Senior Technical Program Manager, you will own the post-sale customer program for a small number of high-stakes enterprise accounts. You are the connective tissue between what customers need and what Ditto delivers.

You'll be managing complex, multi-threaded technical programs: driving implementations to production, translating customer requirements into engineering deliverables, orchestrating internal teams across engineering, product, FDE, and support, and owning the renewal outcome for every account in your portfolio. This role requires someone who can hold their own in a technical conversation with a customer's engineering team in the morning and run a renewal discussion with a VP in the afternoon.

If you've felt constrained by the shallow nature of traditional CSM work, or you want your program management skills to have meaningful commercial impact, this role is the antidote.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Program Delivery

- Build and maintain documented program plans for every assigned account, covering milestones, risks, dependencies, and clear ownership.

- Drive customer implementations from kickoff to production, working backwards from go-live to ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

- Translate customer requirements into actionable engineering deliverables in partnership with Product, Engineering, and FDEs.

- Manage parallel work streams across multiple accounts without losing track of what is at risk.

Cross-Functional Orchestration

- Partner with the AE as a peer, not a support function, proactively keeping them informed of account health, customer sentiment, and any signals that have commercial implications.

- Coordinate across engineering, product, support, and FDE to move customer programs forward without direct authority over any of them.

- Own incident and escalation management end-to-end: route clearly, communicate accurately to the customer, and close the loop.

- Be the single point of accountability for your accounts internally. If something is falling through the cracks, you catch it.

Commercial and Relationship Ownership

- Own renewal outcomes for your portfolio. Renewals should never be a surprise.

- Align with the AE on a shared account narrative. Customers should never experience a gap between what sales told them and what post-sales is executing against.

- Surface expansion signals and route them to the AE with the context needed to act.

- Establish trusted advisor status with customer engineering leads, project managers, and executive sponsors.

- Conduct QBRs and executive business reviews that reflect real program status, not just a health score.

Internal Contribution

- Help refine the playbook. Ditto's enterprise engagement model is actively evolving and this role will contribute to it.

- Contribute structured account intelligence back to product and engineering through the voice of your customers.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

- Demonstrated experience managing complex technical implementations with direct customer-facing accountability
